title: The number of papers

note: The count takes distinct keys in `study_manifest.xlsx`, where Wallsten and Nteta's (2016) studies 4, 5, and 6 carry the keys `wallsten_nteta_2017`, `_2018`, and `_2019` (a spreadsheet autofill). Their `year` and `display_text` columns say 2016. The deposit's `in_text_claims.R` reproduces the printed counts because it reads the same keys.

title: The summary estimate
published: Our random-effects summary estimate is 1.1 points (0–100 scale) with a standard error of 0.8 points
corrected: Our random-effects summary estimate is [[1.2]] points (0–100 scale) with a standard error of 0.8 points
note: The estimate is 1.17 points, and Table 4 prints 0.012. It remains not statistically significant.

title: Half as large
published: the estimated standard deviation is half as large at 2.4 points / with a standard deviation half as large at 2 points
corrected: the estimated standard deviation is [[about two-thirds as large]] at 2.4 points / with a standard deviation [[about two-thirds as large]] at 2 points
note: The two standard deviations are 2.4 and 3.6 points, a ratio of 0.68. The introduction's 2 and 4 are half of one another only as rounded.

title: The significant estimates

corrected: Of the [[9]] significant estimates, 5 (all positive) remain significant
note: The sentence before it counts 8 positive and 1 negative.

title: Studies with other outcomes
published: Among the 10 studies whose treatment comparisons would have met our inclusion criteria but whose outcomes were not political attitudes, we judged five to be inapplicable, four to be consistent with our results
corrected: Among the [[seven]] studies whose treatment comparisons would have met our inclusion criteria but whose outcomes were not political attitudes, we judged [[one]] to be inapplicable, four to be consistent with our results
note: The printed five, four, and two sum to 11. Appendix Table F.47 governs: its "Different outcomes, same treatments" group has 7 rows (1 not applicable, 4 consistent, and 2 inconsistent). The page's "21 such studies" counts the table's rows, one of which collects the candidate choice papers; it stands.

title: Studies by place, and Figure E.12
published: We have 22 studies that randomize a Christian treatment in the United States / 15 total studies in three (sub-Saharan) African countries (Nigeria, Tanzania, and Kenya)
corrected: We have [[21]] studies that randomize a Christian treatment in the United States / [[16]] total studies in [[four]] (sub-Saharan) African countries ([[Burkina Faso,]] Nigeria, Tanzania, and Kenya)
note: Figure E.12 omits Grossman, Nomikos, and Siddiqui's two studies in Burkina Faso, because `countries.csv` spells the country "Burkina" and the study manifest "Burkina Faso", so the join drops them. Its Burkina Faso row should show 2 under Islam, and its United States row correctly shows 21. The figure is not reprinted here. One Nigerian study appears under both traditions, which is why the figure's cells in its three countries sum to 15 where those countries hold 14 studies.

note: 248 is all the reported estimates. The 82% that follows is computed on the 162 omitted ones, and it holds.

title: Standard errors
published: We report HC2 robust standard errors in all cases.
corrected: We report HC2 robust standard errors in [[nearly]] all cases.
note: Severson and Coleman's CATEs by religiosity use HC1, in both the original-scale and standardized scripts, since HC2 is undefined in the high-religiosity group of 8 subjects (leverage at 1). One standardized estimate for Blair et al.'s study 2 also uses HC1.
